item.title: Solutions to Three Spline-Related Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.31314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This AI-assisted article settles (partially) several conjectures coming from spline theory: Scherer--Shadrin conjecture on mirroring the sign patterns of polynomial derivatives is answered in the negative through a counterexample; the author's conjectures on the Lebesgue function of the orthoprojector onto spaces of polynomials multi-vanishing at an endpoint are answered in the affirmative; and Schumaker conjecture on interpolation with lacunary bivariate Bernstein polynomials is provided with solutions in a number of previously unknown situations.
item.dc:creator: Simon Foucart

item.title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.31818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{\alpha,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{\alpha,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.
item.dc:creator: Shengzhe Lu, Qizhen Shen, Fayou Zhao

item.title: Weighted Inequalities for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Trees with Flow Measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.31825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a weighted theory for the fractional Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M_{\mu,\gamma}$, $0<\gamma<1$, on infinite trees equipped with flow measures. Such measures are typically nondoubling and exhibit exponential volume growth, so the classical Muckenhoupt theory does not apply directly. By replacing Euclidean balls with admissible trapezoids, a class of fractional $A(p,q)(\mu)$ weights is introduced, and a Muckenhoupt-type theorem is established: for $1\le p<1/\gamma$ and $1/p-1/q=\gamma$, the operator $M_{\mu,\gamma}$ is bounded from $\ell^p_\mu(\omega^p)$ to $\ell^q_\mu(\omega^q)$ if and only if $\omega\in A(p,q)(\mu)$. The endpoint case $p=1$ is characterized via a weak-type estimate.
item.dc:creator: Shengzhe Lu, Fayou Zhao

item.title: Spectrality of additive measures with Bernoulli convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spectral properties of additive measures of Lebesgue type are by now completely settled \cite{LLP21,ALZ23,KW25,Lu25}. In this paper we continue the study of spectrality for Cantor-type additive measures. For $0<r<1$, let $\mu_r$ denote the Bernoulli convolution generated by the maps $x\mapsto rx$ and $x\mapsto r(x+2)$ with equal weights, and consider the Bernoulli-type additive measure \[ \mu_{r,s}=\tfrac12(\mu_r\times\delta_0+\delta_0\times\mu_s). \] For every even integer $R=2k$ we construct an explicit spectrum of the one-dimensional measure $\mu_{1/R}$, and from it an explicit spectrum of $\mu^{1/R}:=\mu_{1/R,1/R}$ lying on the antidiagonal is constructed. Combined with the recently established absence of Fourier frames for the Bernoulli convolutions $\mu_{1/N}$ for odd integers $N\geq3$ \cite{DLT26,FSW26}, this yields a parity dichotomy: $\mu^{1/R}$ is spectral if and only if $R$ is even. For unequal contraction ratios, we prove that $\mu_{1/2,1/4}$ is not spectral. Several open problems and future directions are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Qiu Mao, Zhi-Yi Wu

item.title: An improved estimate for discrete $L^8$ restriction on the cubic curve
item.description: arXiv:2611.32210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an improved estimate for discrete $L^8$ restriction on the cubic curve $(n,n^3)$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the following eighth moment estimate holds \[ \int_{[0,1]^2} \left|\sum_{n=1}^N b_n \exp(2\pi i(nx+n^3y))\right|^8 dxdy \ll_{\varepsilon} N^{1/2-1/47500+\varepsilon} \left(\sum_{n=1}^N |b_n|^2\right)^4. \]
item.dc:creator: Xudong Lai, Hongxu Wu

item.title: A characterization of almost everywhere convergence of subsequences of Walsh--Fourier partial sums
item.description:
arXiv:2611.32362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the increasing sequences $(
u_j)$ in the set of positive integers $\mathbb N$ along which the Walsh--Fourier partial sums $s_{
u_j}(f)$ of every integrable function $f$ converge almost everywhere to $f$. This resolves a problem that Konyagin posed in his invited address at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians~\cite{K06}. The criterion concerns the binary expansions of the integers $
u_j$. Divide each $
u_j$ by $2^k$. Convergence holds if and only if, for some $K\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct positive quotients whose remainder has binary variation larger than $K$ is bounded independently of the scale $k$. This is also equivalent to the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for $\sup_{j\in\mathbb N}|s_{
u_j}(f)|$, and if the criterion fails, then the partial sums of some integrable function along $(
u_j)$ are unbounded at every point. The criterion contains the bounded variation condition and Konyagin's condition for separated spectra, and we give examples, for convergence and for divergence, that are not covered by the earlier results.
item.dc:creator: Weisz Ferenc, Guangheng Xie, Dachun Yang

item.title: Hardy and BMO spaces for the Laplacian with drift
item.description: arXiv:2611.32470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Hardy and BMO spaces associated with the Laplacian with drift. We define an atomic Hardy space $H^1$ whose atoms satisfy cancellation against constants and linear functions in directions perpendicular to the drift. We prove the John--Nirenberg inequality, Hardy--BMO duality, equivalence of finite and infinite atomic norms, and interpolation theorems. We show that the Riesz transforms and their adjoints are bounded from $H^1$ to $L^1$ and from $L^\infty$ to BMO. Moreover, we prove that the cancellation conditions are optimal, but the Riesz transforms do not characterize $H^1$. We also characterize the $L^p$ boundedness of their commutators, $1<p<\infty$, in terms of local BMO.
item.dc:creator: The Anh Bui, Fu Ken Ly

item.title: On the maximal operator of the hybrid Hermite-Laguerre-Jacobi semigroup
item.description: arXiv:2611.32492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the heat-diffusion semigroup related to expansions with respect to an orthogonal system emerging by taking arbitrary finite tensor products of classical Hermite, Laguerre and Jacobi polynomials. Our main result is the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the associated maximal operator. This implies pointwise almost everywhere boundary convergence of the semigroup to initial values for all initial conditions that are integrable against the orthogonality measure.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nowak

item.title: Optimal polynomial meshes on quasicircles via conformal scale comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.32577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every quasicircle $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{C}$ admits an optimal admissible polynomial mesh for univariate complex polynomials. More precisely, if $E$ denotes the closed Jordan domain bounded by $\Gamma$, then for every $\Lambda>1$ there are finite sets $A_n\subset\Gamma$ with $\mathrm{card}(A_n)=O(n)$ and $\|p\|_E=\|p\|_\Gamma\leq\Lambda\|p\|_{A_n}$ for every $p\in\mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{C})$. The nodes may be chosen as images of equally spaced points of the unit circle under the inverse exterior conformal map, equivalently as equal-mass points for harmonic measure at infinity. The proof combines the classical conformal level-curve scale with a discrete norming principle. If $\rho_n(z)$ denotes the distance from a boundary point to the exterior level curve $|\Phi|=1+1/n$, Bernstein--Walsh and Cauchy's formula show that any sufficiently fine $\rho_n$-net is norming. A scale-comparison property then turns $O(n)$ equally spaced angular samples into such a net. Quasicircles satisfy this property by quasisymmetry. The argument requires no smoothness or rectifiability and applies in particular to the classical von Koch snowflake.
item.dc:creator: Dami\'an Pinasco, Juan Pablo Pinasco, Mar\'ia Victoria Venuti

item.title: Sharp variational estimates for Schr\"odinger equation in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study strong $r$-variation estimates for the free Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$. Combining fractal and weighted restriction estimates with mixed space--time estimates, we determine the sharp Sobolev regularity, up to endpoints, in several ranges of the spatial exponent $p$ and the variation exponent $r$. In particular, our results give a sharp $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ variational extension of the Schr\"odinger maximal estimate of Du and Zhang [\emph{Ann. of Math.}, \textbf{189}, 837--861 (2019)].
item.dc:creator: Chen Yanping, Tang Yongrui

item.title: An $A_1$ characterization of the boundedness of the maximal function on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces for exponents satisfying $1<p_-\le p_+<\infty$. We show that $M$ is bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}_w$ if and only if the pair $(p(\cdot),w)$ satisfies a variable Muckenhoupt condition and there exists $h\in L^1$ such that $w^{-1}h^{1/p(\cdot)}$ and $wh^{1/p'(\cdot)}$ belong to $A_1$. This characterization is new even in the unweighted setting. To prove sufficiency, we use sparse domination together with a local modular averaging estimate whose error terms are summable over sparse families to $\|h\|_{L^1}$. Conversely, assuming $M$ is bounded, we construct $h$ using a simultaneous Rubio de Francia algorithm. To motivate this new characterization, we show that the strong Muckenhoupt condition, which characterizes the boundedness of $M$ in the unweighted case by a theorem of Diening, is not sufficient in the weighted setting. As applications, we give short proofs and extensions of known sufficient conditions.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Gon\c{c}alves, Tuomas Oikari, Troy Roberts

item.title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
item.description: arXiv:2611.31447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carath\'{e}odory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.
item.dc:creator: Wolfram Bauer, Zhicheng Han, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2611.31827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton series. With it we show that, near a root of the Alexander polynomial, the rescaled analytic interpolation converges to Gaussian and Scorer-type profiles, uniformly for complex values of the rescaled color, and we determine how fast the rank may grow before these limits change. Finally, continuation in $\log q$ produces a logarithmic monodromy whose coefficient is a convergent pairing of the same Borel residues that give the Stokes jump. For the figure-eight knot, the asymptotics of this coefficient are governed by the hyperbolic volume at every rank.
item.dc:creator: Honghuai Fang

item.title: Analytic properties of distributions associated with multi-state Random Number Generators
item.description: arXiv:2611.31842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the analytic properties of probability distributions associated with possibly unfair, multi-state Random Number Generators (i.e., dice). Specifically, given a $q$-sided die, if $x_i\in \{0,\ldots, q-1\}$ denotes the outcome of the $i^{\text{th}}$ toss, then $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]$ is the associated cumulative distribution function---a probabilistic generalization of the famed Cantor function. We first establish easily computable bounds for the $L^1$-distance between the possibly unfair $F$ and the uniform distribution $y=x$. We then show that $F$ is both upper- and lower-H\"{o}lder continuous, where the associated H\"{o}lder exponents are shown to be sharp. Finally, we establish recursive formulae for the moments, $\mathbb{E}[X^n]$, associated with $F$ and use these moments to provide sequences of step-functions that converge uniformly to $F$ from above and below.
item.dc:creator: Douglas T. Pfeffer, Volodymyr Zabolotnyi

item.title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.31845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^\gamma$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^\gamma$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^\gamma$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^\gamma$ on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all $0 < \gamma \leq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Chenghao Xiang, Fayou Zhao

item.title: Relaxation dynamics of Winfree oscillators on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.32179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study exponential relaxation to equilibrium for Winfree-type models on Riemannian manifolds. For the sphere model with entrainment point $p$ and canonical influence, we derive convergence to equilibrium, whenever no oscillator starts at the antipode $-p$. For the corresponding canonical model on $\mathrm U(d)$, we obtain the same convergence whenever no initial matrix has the eigenvalue $-1$. Both results hold above explicit coupling thresholds depending on the initial configuration and the frequency matrices. For a broader class of unitary influence functions, the same spectral condition yields exponential convergence for sufficiently large coupling strengths. Finite-time entrance into positively invariant stable regions and contraction estimates yield exponential convergence rates and equilibrium uniqueness within those regions. A finite symmetry construction on Lie groups realizes the unitary model and a special unitary analogue as invariant Kuramoto--Lohe subsystems, yielding local relaxation results. Finally, we formulate an abstract Winfree model on Riemannian manifolds and establish local exponential relaxation in a fixed coordinate neighborhood under quantitative attraction and regularity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Seung-Yeal Ha, Chaejoo Lee, Eunjun Lee, Jaemoon Lee, Seung-Yeon Ryoo

item.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16294v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet $L^2$-norm. The zero-dimensional case yields a large-value estimate on $R^{1/2}$-cubes. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: Sharp estimates for imaginary powers of discrete Laplacians
item.description: arXiv:2610.27385v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Delta_{\rm d}$ be the nonnegative discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb Z^d$. We prove that, for $0<p\le1$, \[ \|\Delta_{\rm d}^{i\gamma}\|_{H^p_{\Delta_{\rm d}}\to H^p_{\Delta_{\rm d}}} \lesssim (1+|\gamma|)^{d(1/p-1/2)}, \] and, for $1<p<\infty$, \[ \|\Delta_{\rm d}^{i\gamma}\|_{\ell^p\to\ell^p} \lesssim (1+|\gamma|)^{d|1/p-1/2|}. \] The estimates are sharp with respect to the exponent of $1+|\gamma|$. We also explain why the general spectral multiplier theorem and the usual Calder\'on--Zygmund approach do not give the sharp power.
item.dc:creator: The Anh Bui, The Quan Bui, Thanh Tinh Cao

item.title: Sharpness of the Martin-O'Bryant autoconvolution inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.12685v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that there does not exist a constant $c<1$ such that ${\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{2}}^2\le c\,{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{1}}{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{\infty}}$ holds for every nonnegative $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})\cap L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
item.dc:creator: Ton\'{c}i Crmari\'{c}, Vjekoslav Kova\v{c}, Jelena Rup\v{c}i\'{c}

item.title: On discrete harmonic functions with non-negativity on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An improvement of Liouville's theorem for harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ was obtained by Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin. Namely, they proved that if a discrete harmonic function is bounded on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then the function is constant. In this paper, we prove the corresponding result if we replace the boundedness assumption with non-negativity.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Gaitan Montejo, Carlos Garz\'on, Jos\'e Madrid

item.title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
item.description: arXiv:2611.26113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the multiplicity of positive solutions of the following Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \begin{aligned} \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' +a(t)g(u)&=0,\quad t\in(0,T),\\ u'(0)=u'(T)&=0, \end{aligned} \] where $a$ is a two-step sign-changing weight with negative mean. We establish a multiplicity criterion for positive solutions, give a negative answer to the uniqueness question raised by Boscaggin, Feltrin and Zanolin, and prove the existence of infinitely many positive solutions for a fixed weight. The proofs are based on the shooting method and uniform asymptotic estimates.
item.dc:creator: Ao Xiao

item.title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
item.description: arXiv:2611.30274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: Sharp double logarithmic Brezis-Gallou\"et-Wainger inequalities in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:1301.2353v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The space $H^2(\mathbb{R}^4)$ is not contained in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^4)$. For functions in $H^2_0$ of the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are also H\"older continuous of order $\alpha$, the supremum norm can nevertheless be controlled by the $L^2$ norm of the Laplacian, at the cost of a logarithm of the H\"older seminorm. We determine the optimal leading constant in this estimate. With a double logarithmic correction, the optimal constant is $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. With a single logarithm, the estimate holds for every larger constant and fails for $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$ itself. No symmetry assumption is made. The proof reduces the question to a biharmonic obstacle problem with an obstacle of H\"older type. Its minimizer is radial and explicit, and the sharp constant is determined by the asymptotic behaviour of the free boundary radius. We also derive versions of these inequalities on balls and on the whole space. The results are second-order analogues in dimension four of the two-dimensional inequalities of Ibrahim, Majdoub and Masmoudi.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni

item.title: On $\beta=6$ Tracy-Widom distribution and the second Calogero-Painlev\'e system
item.description: arXiv:2010.06733v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Calogero-Painlev\'e systems were introduced in 2001 by K. Takasaki as a natural generalization of the classical Painlev\'e equations to the case of the several Painlev\'e ``particles'' coupled via the Calogero type interactions. In 2014, I. Rumanov discovered the remarkable fact that a particular case of the second Calogero-Painlev\'e II equation describes the Tracy-Widom distribution function for the general beta-ensembles with even values of the parameter beta. Most recently, in 2017 work of M. Bertola, M. Cafasso, and V. Rubtsov, it was proven that all Calogero-Painlev\'e systems are Lax integrable, and hence their solutions admit a Riemann-Hilbert representation. This important observation has opened the door to rigorous, based on the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method, asymptotic analysis of the Calogero-Painlev\'e equations. This in turn yields the possibility of rigorous evaluation of the asymptotic behavior of the Tracy-Widom distributions for the values of beta beyond the classical $\beta =1, 2, 4.$ In this work we shall start an asymptotic analysis of the Calogero-Painlev\'e system with a special focus on the Calogero-Painlev\'e system corresponding to $\beta = 6$ Tracy-Widom distribution function. The principle technical challenge is the implementation of the nonlinear steepest descent approach beyond the $2\times 2$ matrix dimension of the corresponding Riemann-Hilbert problem; in our case, it is $6\times 6$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Its, Andrei Prokhorov

item.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
item.description: arXiv:2601.01348v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve with interior and exterior domains $\Omega_i$ and $\Omega_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study harmonic functions $u$ on either domain $\Omega$ with finite weighted energy $\int_\Omega |\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma)^{(1-s)p-1} dA(z)$. On the unit circle, the interior and exterior trace spaces both coincide with the fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(\Gamma)$. We ask which rough curves preserve this trace identity and the corresponding seminorm estimates. For radial-Lipschitz curves, we prove that both trace spaces coincide with $B^s_{p,p}(\Gamma)$, with equivalent seminorms, in the following ranges: $1/p-1/2\le s<1$ for $1<p<2$; $0<s<1$ for $p=2$; and $0<s\le 1/p+1/2$ for $2<p<\infty$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same conclusion holds when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle on radial-Lipschitz domains: for $4/3\le p\le 4$, the unweighted $p$-energy of the harmonic extension is bounded by a constant times that of any extension with the same boundary values. Neither endpoint can be improved over this class. We also obtain a sharp endpoint counterpart of Brennan's integrability conclusion: every Riemann map $g$ from a bounded radial-Lipschitz domain $\Omega_i$ onto the unit disk satisfies $g'\in L^4(\Omega_i)$, and no exponent greater than $4$ works for all such domains.
item.dc:creator: Huaying Wei, Michel Zinsmeister
